html:
The Qutb Minar is a tall stone tower of victory and minaret in south Delhi, begun around 1199 by Qutb ud-Din Aibak and finished by his successor Iltutmish.

It stands about 73 metres high in five storeys of red and buff sandstone and marble, with bands of carved Arabic writing and balconies at each level. It was the tallest building in India for centuries. Lightning damaged the top in the 14th century, and Firuz Shah Tughlaq rebuilt the upper storeys.

It marked the arrival of the new rulers after the Second Battle of Tarain. Beside it stands the Quwwat al-Islam mosque, the first mosque in Delhi, built partly with columns taken from Hindu and Jain temples on the site. In the mosque courtyard stands the much older Iron Pillar, from the Gupta age.

The tower may have been inspired by the Minaret of Jam in the Ghurid homeland in Afghanistan. It is now a World Heritage Site and a symbol of the Delhi Sultanate.
sum: The Qutb Minar is a tall stone tower of victory and minaret in south Delhi, begun around 1199 by Qutb ud-Din Aibak and finished by his successor Iltutmish.
